annotation.title_clean: Decision No. 1412/2023 Issuing the Regulation Governing Unmanned Aircraft Systems (Drones)
annotation.title_en: Decision No. 1412/2023 Issuing the Regulation Governing Unmanned Aircraft Systems (Drones)
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Civil Aviation Authority, Sultanate of Oman (Ministry of Transport, Communications and Information Technology)
annotation.summary_en: Omani Civil Aviation Authority regulation (Decision 1412/2023) governing drones: registration, licensing, operating obligations and prohibitions, licensee liability, and administrative fines. It repeals the 2020 drone regulation and exempts military and security agencies within their duties.
key_provisions_or_claims: All drones must be registered; flying activities and aerial work require a license, with exemptions for indoor use and toy drones up to 250 g.
License requires age 18 or Omani registration, third-party liability insurance, training/exam, and an operational permit.
Operations must be within visual line of sight or use authorized tracking and collision avoidance, below 120 m.
Prohibits flights within 5 km of airports or protected places, night flights without authorization, weaponization, and privacy invasion.
Licensee is liable for damage; fines of OMR 200-600 are doubled for repeat offenses, with license revocation possible.
